text:
Maria P.: Weekly GPU capacity snapshot — dropping the short version here. Key bullets: APAC demand up ~22% week-over-week, eu-west has intermittent network issues impacting one cluster, and NYC pools are at ~88% committed. Please skim and flag blockers.

Chris L.: Where's the sheet? can you paste the 6-week burn numbers?

Maria P.: pasted tiny extract below for quick context:
```
region    cluster       projected_gpu_hours_w1  w2   w3
us-east   cluster-nyc-1  12,400                13k  13,500
us-west   cluster-sf-2   7,200                 7.5k 7,800
apac      cluster-sg-3   5,600                 6.8k 7,200
eu-west   cluster-eu2    4,900                 5.1k 5,300
```

Devon R.: Heads up — cluster-eu2 had 3 node reboots and a BGP flap overnight, saw packet drops ~2:14am UTC. short log: `2026-06-14T02:14:12Z kubelet: node reboot detected -> recovered`

autoscale-bot: autoscaler: scaled cluster-eu2 by +8 GPUs at 2026-06-14T03:05:10Z (policy: emergency-burst)

Sophie (oncall): For eu-west we should hold a maintenance window. Network team said they're rolling a firmware patch tomorrow 0200-0300 UTC. We should avoid rollouts around that. @devon can you confirm rollback hooks are set for canaries?

Devon R.: rollback hooks in place for canaries. but if patch causes transient route changes, warm caches will suffer. recommend we pre-warm KV cache before peak and bump ephemeral buffer to 30% for 2 hours post-patch.

Chris L.: If we follow that plan, what's the extra cost? ballpark numbers?

Maria P.: Rough math = ~120 GPU hours extra during warm window for eu-west -> ~$3.6k one-time + ongoing model serving overhead ~$4k/mo if we keep buffer. For APAC surge (22%) — adds ~1.2k GPU hours/week -> ~$18k/mo if we increase reserved by 10%.

Sophie (oncall): Given SLA risk, I vote we take the safety buffer in APAC and pre-warm eu-west. Ops prefers predictable cost over outages. :thumbsup:

Chris L.: Alternative: shift less latency-sensitive batch jobs from APAC to us-west on nights (non-overlapping windows). That frees ~150 GPU hours/day. Might reduce reserved need.

Devon R.: That could work, but requires changing scheduler priorities + adjusting retry/backoff. I can prototype a quick spot-preemptible fallback that moves low-priority jobs. May add ~10% retry cost.

Maria P.: Action items: 1) I'll update the forecast with +10% APAC reserved and an eu-west pre-warm line item (ETA EOD). 2) @Devon prototype batch-shift plan (PR by Wed). 3) @Sophie schedule maintenance window with network and set no-rollout policy.

Sophie (oncall): On it. I'll create an incident-style ticket and tag the network team.

Chris L.: SGTM. Thanks all.

Maria P.: Thanks — I'll ping sales/partners about the SLA buffer so they know about potential cost changes. :wave:
